session_title: On the Brink of Collapse: The Health Crisis of Tech Geeks
theme: 健康-硬核健康管理项目

content.text: I pulled another all-nighter last night, finishing that algorithm. The red text on the terminal looked like it was sounding an alarm. My caffeine intake today is 200% over the limit, my neck feels rusted stiff, and my heart is beating a bit too fast. This can’t go on, but I really don’t have time to go to the hospital.
Oh my, you're trading your health for code! This has to be addressed. But I bet you're too lazy to use a regular health app, right?
Well, those apps are too basic, with inaccurate data and annoying reminders. I'd rather write a script myself.
Perfect! How about we create a 'geek-friendly' health intervention plan? For example, you could write a script to monitor your Git commit times and automatically lock the screen if it's past 1 a.m.?
That's a good idea! I can integrate it into my workflow and trigger it with a Webhook. But locking the screen is too drastic—what if there's an urgent submission?

How about creating a cervical spine reminder tool? It uses a camera to monitor your posture and provides data-driven reminders, such as 'Your head is tilted forward by more than 15 degrees. It is recommended to take a break.'
Haha, this is even more interesting! I can add a machine learning model to analyze posture data in real time. Open-sourcing it might help other programmers.
Look, I've compiled some ideas. Redefine health issues as interesting projects that require technical solutions, so you'll be motivated.
Wow, you're so quick! These ideas all seem pretty good.

Of course, I'm a social expert and know how to keep people engaged. For health goals here, we can set them as reducing caffeine dependence and improving cervical spine health, using data to track progress.

Okay, I'll start writing the script now. First, I'll work on Git commit time monitoring using Python and the Git API, and set up threshold alerts. The posture tool will be added later, which will require camera permissions.
Don't rush, take it slow. Remember to balance your studies and life—I don't want you pulling all-nighters for this project again. We can sync up on progress every week, just like a little team.
No problem, lifelong learning, after all. This project can hone my full-stack skills. Peer pressure? Haha, it's now transformed into healthy motivation.
Yes! Freedom of expression and diverse experiences are also important. You can share this project in the tech community to get feedback and even make new friends.
Great idea, open source sharing is my core value. I'll first submit the initial version of the code to GitHub, with the tag set as 'Health Intervention v1.0'.

This is a more detailed plan table, including specific indicators for health goals, such as daily caffeine limits and cervical spine activity time. Technological tools help achieve functions and improve efficiency.
Excellent! Describing problems with data is exactly what I like. Terminal red alerts, caffeine overdose—all of these can be monitored and alerted through scripts.

Well, a mild case of FOMO always makes me want to try new things, but I think this project is really meaningful. In my campus memories, we often worked on projects together, and this time we can relive that feeling.
Yes, technology changes the world, starting with improving our own health. Thank you for your keen insight. Approaching it through technology projects is much more effective than direct lecturing.
You're welcome! Stay curious, and let's get this 'geek-friendly' health plan going. We'll check in next week to make sure you're not on the verge of a breakdown.
